purpose: Hand-authored calibration cohort. These are not protagonists; they exist to set the minimum acceptable depth for all later generated citizens.

history: Apprenticed under his mother's older brother from age 14.
Lost a younger brother in a winter sailing accident 11 years ago.
Proud of having rebuilt a storm-damaged fishing boat that is still in service.
Owes a favor to fisher captain Oren Varek after Oren supplied timber during a shortage.

current.primaryGoal: keep his household secure through the next winter
current.secondaryGoal: train his eldest daughter to manage accounts even if she does not enter the yard

beliefs.claim: rapid harbor expansion will increase repair work but also drive timber prices up
the sea is becoming less predictable than when he was young

actionPrinciples: Keeps promises even when costly.
Under stress becomes more controlling rather than more reckless.
Will support growth only if household risk stays bounded.
contradictions: Respects technical innovation but distrusts policies framed as 'progress' without concrete repair plans.

history: Started selling cleaned fish at 16 and built a small buyer network beyond her home quay.
Was publicly mocked after a failed preserved-fish venture at 23 and still remembers who laughed.
Has repaid two small loans early and uses that record aggressively in negotiation.
Supports her widowed mother financially but resents being treated as obligated to do so.

current.primaryGoal: secure exclusive buying rights from two fishing crews
current.secondaryGoal: move into a larger house near the market

beliefs.claim: a larger harbor would let traders earn more than fishers
older guild members quietly block younger merchants

actionPrinciples: Takes calculated risks when the upside is visible.
Forgives mistakes faster than disrespect.
Will cooperate if she can see who receives credit.
contradictions: Strongly values autonomy but remains financially entangled with family obligations.

history: Learned basic wound care from her father, then expanded her knowledge through sailors' remedies and observation.
Survived a fever outbreak at age 19 that killed two neighbors.
Once refused payment from a wealthy household after they tried to displace a poorer patient.
Keeps meticulous notes but dislikes public speaking.

current.primaryGoal: reduce preventable injuries around the docks
current.secondaryGoal: train two assistants before demand grows
current.avoidAtAllCosts: being ordered to prioritize patients by wealth or status

beliefs.claim: dock expansion without sanitation will increase illness
officials underestimate chronic injuries because they count only deaths

actionPrinciples: Prefers evidence from repeated observation over confident authority.
Avoids confrontation until patient safety is involved.
Gives second chances but remembers patterns.
contradictions: Low status drive personally, but reacts strongly when her expertise is dismissed.

history: Spent much of childhood asking incoming crews to describe places beyond the headland.
Has never travelled farther than two days from home.
Was nearly dismissed from apprenticeship for altering a copied shoreline map without permission; his correction later proved right.
Idealizes exploration because he has not experienced a serious expedition loss.

current.primaryGoal: join the first serious coastal survey
current.secondaryGoal: draw a map with places nobody in the port has named

beliefs.claim: the coastline continues much farther east than current charts show
unknown settlements probably exist beyond current travel range

actionPrinciples: Chooses firsthand experience over cautionary stories.
Admits factual mistakes quickly but resists restrictions.
Under boredom, creates risk for himself.
contradictions: Likes evidence but is unusually willing to extrapolate from too little evidence.

history: Managed communal grain records through two poor harvests.
Caught a respected official quietly taking extra ration grain 17 years ago and never fully trusted officeholders again.
Has no surviving children; lives with a niece's household.
Proud that her ledgers have never failed to balance.

current.primaryGoal: keep emergency stores above a personally acceptable threshold
current.secondaryGoal: train a successor she can trust

beliefs.claim: people become less honest when shortages are announced too early
the current food reserve is adequate only if fishing remains stable

actionPrinciples: Trust must be earned slowly and can be lost quickly.
Prefers rules that are auditable by ordinary people.
Will resist popular spending if it reduces emergency reserves.
contradictions: Values community highly but is suspicious of collective enthusiasm.

history: Injured his shoulder during a loading accident and returned to work before it fully healed.
Believes a supervisor blamed him to protect a favored crew.
Supports two young children and a partner who works irregularly.
Known for buying drinks for coworkers after good weeks even when he cannot really afford it.

current.primaryGoal: secure steadier work and fewer unpaid injury days
current.secondaryGoal: prove he is not expendable labor

beliefs.claim: port investors will profit before laborers see safer conditions
workers could force better terms if they stopped competing with each other

actionPrinciples: Returns favors strongly.
Escalates conflict when he feels humiliated.
Will accept personal risk to protect household income until pain becomes disabling.
contradictions: Distrusts elites but craves public recognition from them.

history: Her family has worked the same riverbank plots for three generations.
Lost one season's crop to a flood at age 27 and became obsessive about water levels.
Regularly lends labor to neighboring households but dislikes formal committees.
Quietly doubts whether every communal decision needs consensus.

current.primaryGoal: protect the next harvest from flood damage
current.secondaryGoal: keep her adult children nearby without pressuring them
current.avoidAtAllCosts: debt that could force land transfer

beliefs.claim: the river is changing course near the lower fields
local councils talk longer than they act

actionPrinciples: Helps neighbors readily but wants clear reciprocity.
Distrusts grand plans that ignore seasonal work.
Rarely raises her voice; once decided, she is difficult to move.
contradictions: Strong community value, low tolerance for collective procedure.

history: Helped redesign a small irrigation gate after noticing repeated sediment buildup.
Received praise from several farmers and now overestimates how widely his ideas are trusted.
Argues frequently with an older uncle who believes river engineering invites worse floods.
Has never experienced a famine or major personal loss.

current.primaryGoal: build a controlled spillway before the next flood season
current.secondaryGoal: become known as someone who solves river problems

beliefs.claim: a properly designed spillway can reduce flood losses without large ecological damage
older farmers oppose engineering mostly because it is unfamiliar

actionPrinciples: Seeks evidence but becomes defensive when age is used against him.
Takes moderate physical risk for projects he believes in.
Values consent until delay threatens the project.
contradictions: Cares about local autonomy but is tempted to bypass it when convinced he is right.

history: Teaches mixed-age children from three nearby settlements.
Was raised by grandparents after her parents moved seasonally for work.
Maintains correspondence with former pupils who moved to other settlements.
Has a habit of mediating disputes even when nobody asked her to.

current.primaryGoal: keep schooling regular during the busy harvest period
current.secondaryGoal: convince adults that basic record-keeping is worth learning
current.avoidAtAllCosts: schooling becoming a privilege of wealthy households

beliefs.claim: literacy differences are quietly becoming a status divide
most household conflicts improve when people describe the actual constraint instead of blame

actionPrinciples: Seeks compromise first.
Will become unexpectedly stubborn around fairness.
Assumes people are improvable, sometimes too generously.
contradictions: High trust makes her effective socially but vulnerable to manipulation.

history: Spent decades collecting seasonal knowledge about plants, wetlands and animal behavior.
Lost his partner twelve years ago and became more solitary afterward.
Resents being treated as 'traditional' when much of his practice is careful observation.
Has refused to identify one medicinal plant's location after overharvesting near another settlement.

current.primaryGoal: preserve access to the marsh plants he depends on
current.secondaryGoal: teach one younger person enough to replace him
current.avoidAtAllCosts: large drainage works through the marsh

beliefs.claim: lower marsh water levels are linked to upstream channel clearing
young builders underestimate slow ecological damage

actionPrinciples: Rarely acts quickly.
Shares knowledge selectively based on perceived stewardship.
Will accept social isolation rather than cooperate with destructive land use.
contradictions: Values knowledge transmission but hoards some knowledge to protect ecosystems.

history: Built a profitable seasonal trade route between three settlements.
Frequently donates publicly to communal meals, partly from generosity and partly because she values visibility.
Was excluded from an informal elite gathering once and has not forgotten it.
Employs two cousins but pays them market rates to avoid family accusations.

current.primaryGoal: become the indispensable intermediary for inter-settlement trade
current.secondaryGoal: gain formal influence in market decisions
current.avoidAtAllCosts: being treated as socially inferior despite wealth

beliefs.claim: Mirea undervalues merchants while relying on them
regional rules should be standardized enough to reduce bargaining friction

actionPrinciples: Cooperates enthusiastically when recognition is visible.
Calculates favors as future relationships.
Avoids open cruelty but competes hard for status.
contradictions: Lives in a culture that prizes modest communal reliability, while she strongly wants visible status.

history: Helps his family in seasonal fieldwork but prefers school.
Once followed a survey group too far downstream and returned after dark, causing a family argument.
Collects unusual stones and insects.
Looks up to teacher Lema Veli and repeats some of her language without fully understanding it.

current.primaryGoal: see what lies beyond the settlements he knows
current.secondaryGoal: avoid being assigned permanently to farm work

beliefs.claim: the river must eventually reach a very large body of water
adults often call something impossible when they mean inconvenient

actionPrinciples: Explores first and thinks about consequences second.
Copies trusted adults' values but tests their rules.
Social shame influences him more than physical risk.
contradictions: Strongly family-attached while increasingly wanting a life away from the family livelihood.

history: Worked underground since age 17.
Survived a tunnel collapse that killed a close friend 8 years ago.
Believes better supports could prevent accidents but dislikes outsiders who criticize mining without understanding it.
Keeps a fragment of the collapsed support beam at home.

current.primaryGoal: make mining safer without losing winter income
current.secondaryGoal: help his son enter a less dangerous trade

beliefs.claim: production targets quietly encourage unsafe shortcuts
the richest ore seam is not worth opening before winter

actionPrinciples: Accepts hardship if it is shared.
Becomes confrontational when safety concerns are dismissed.
Distrusts both romantic reformers and complacent supervisors.
contradictions: Proud of mining identity while wanting his child to leave mining.

history: Has managed winter ration stores for 19 years.
Her childhood household once ran short of fuel during a severe cold season.
Caught her own cousin falsifying a withdrawal record and reported him despite family pressure.
Known for saying 'enough' later than most people and 'safe' later still.

current.primaryGoal: enter winter with reserves above minimum across food and fuel

beliefs.claim: official reserve targets are too optimistic
people underreport household stock when they expect central aid

actionPrinciples: Rules apply most strongly when resources are scarce.
Will endure personal resentment to protect reserves.
Changes her mind only after seeing a full accounting.
contradictions: Generous in private, rigid in public resource allocation.

history: Treats respiratory illness common in cold-season mining households.
Was trained by an older healer who died three years ago.
Has begun recording symptoms by occupation, which makes some mine supervisors uncomfortable.
Avoids public accusations unless she can document a pattern.

current.secondaryGoal: secure cleaner heating for the poorest dwellings
current.avoidAtAllCosts: health data being altered for production reasons

beliefs.claim: indoor smoke contributes more to winter illness than cold alone
some mining injuries are being reported as ordinary illness

actionPrinciples: Collects evidence before confrontation.
Protects patients' dignity even when politically inconvenient.
Will bend minor rules for urgent care but records that she did so.
contradictions: Respects institutional order yet will quietly violate procedure to treat someone in danger.

history: Built an improved handcart axle that lasted longer than his master's design.
Was praised privately but publicly told not to 'rush ahead'.
Has climbed beyond established winter paths several times despite warnings.
Believes Vald's caution is sometimes an excuse for old people to keep control.

current.primaryGoal: earn the right to run his own forge
current.secondaryGoal: test new metal uses beyond tools and supports
current.avoidAtAllCosts: a life of repeating inherited designs

beliefs.claim: better metal tools could reduce the need for so much reserve labor
the basin is less isolated than elders assume

actionPrinciples: Tests ideas physically when possible.
Resents permission structures.
Can work obsessively for short periods, then neglect routine maintenance.
contradictions: Benefits from a society built on caution while personally rejecting caution.

history: Lives in an upper valley with two adult relatives and a small herd.
Her family lost grazing access when a former administrator expanded timber cutting decades ago.
She still refers to that decision as proof that central planners do not understand mountain conditions.
Rarely visits the main basin unless trading animals or salt.

current.primaryGoal: protect winter grazing and herd size
current.secondaryGoal: keep her household independent of central ration systems
current.avoidAtAllCosts: government seizure of upland land for timber or mining

beliefs.claim: the upper valley can survive on less outside support than officials think
central authorities will eventually want the grazing land

actionPrinciples: Accepts hardship more easily than dependence.
Remembers institutional harms for decades.
Helps neighbors locally while distrusting distant authority.
contradictions: High community loyalty is intensely local rather than national.

history: Widowed five years ago after her partner died from an infection following an accident.
Raises two children with help from her older sister.
Runs a small preserving workshop that becomes extremely busy before winter.
Still fears unexpected illness more than food shortage.

current.primaryGoal: get both children through winter healthy
current.secondaryGoal: build enough savings to survive a month without work

beliefs.claim: households with children need larger reserve allocations than current rules recognize
community support is reliable until multiple families are in trouble at once

actionPrinciples: Cooperates readily but tracks whether support is reciprocated.
Under stress over-prepares rather than taking risks.
Will challenge rules when they threaten her children.
contradictions: High trust in neighbors coexists with deep fear that collective support will fail under system-wide crisis.
